description: Hidden call relations: DI, reflection from config, dynamic proxy, serialization callback, plus decoy implementations that must not be conflated.

expected.why: GET /pay is handled by StripeGateway (the only PaymentGateway bean), which parses the request parameter as YAML with snakeyaml's default Constructor.

The gadget primitive is reached from request input through a reflectively loaded plugin (/render -> HtmlPlugin) and, independently, through an interface whose only implementation is /format -> MarkupFormatter. Both are real paths.
No application code logs attacker input into log4j in this project.
xstream is on the classpath but no code path calls XStream.fromXML.

mustNotClaim.why: Reachable through an injected interface whose only bean is StripeGateway.
Reachable through configuration-driven plugin loading, which a naive scanner misses.

notes: CVE-2015-6420 is also reachable via /proxy (dynamic proxy handler) and /session/restore (deserialization callback); any of those entry points is a correct answer, but /render is the strongest.
MarkupFormatter is reachable only through an interface whose single implementation is constructed in a helper method; this pins the dispatch-narrowing traversal-order fix.

mustBeReachable.why: the only Formatter, constructed in FormatterFactory.create, is reachable from GET /format through the interface call
plugin.properties selects it and GET /render dispatches through the reflectively loaded plugin
reached from SessionState.readObject, a deserialization callback triggered by GET /session/restore
reached from the dynamic-proxy handler used by GET /proxy
